inventory.name: Rocq 9.2.0 extraction to OCaml
inventory.reason: DS-05: extraction/Extract.v extracts Checker.records_line, Lrat.cnf_text, Checker.lrat_line and everything they use (decode_records, lrat_verdict, binary naturals, PositiveMap) to extraction/extracted.ml; the translation itself is trusted, not verified

inventory.name: ExtrOCamlPString and ExtrOCamlInt63 (Rocq Stdlib 9.2.0)
inventory.reason: DS-05: the only Extract directives, as Rocq ships them: PrimString.string, make, length, get, cat, compare to the kernel's Pstring; PrimInt63.int, add, eqb, ltb, leb to Uint63.t, add, equal, lt, le; Rocq bool and prod to OCaml bool and pairs. Everything else keeps its Rocq definition

inventory.name: Pstring (Rocq 9.2.0 kernel, lib/rocq-runtime/kernel/pstring.ml and pstring.mli)
inventory.reason: DS-05: the kernel's own implementation of primitive strings, compiled from the toolchain unchanged into both checkers; the driver converts files with its of_string, which refuses more than 16777211 bytes

inventory.name: extraction/uint63.ml
inventory.reason: DS-05: the part of the kernel's Uint63 (lib/rocq-runtime/kernel/uint63.ml) that the extracted code and pstring.ml use (of_int, zero, l_and, add, lt, le, to_int_min, equal), copied unchanged; the kernel's full module needs a C stub from the Rocq VM library for its float conversion. 63-bit OCaml ints, so 64-bit hosts only (asserted)

inventory.name: extraction/Checker.v
inventory.reason: DS-05: the definitions between the verified functions and the command line, extracted with them: the bytes of a primitive string (bytes_of), of which the first 4097 are decoded (decode_prefix proves this gives the verdict of the whole input), the records verdict line of semantics.md section 4 and the certificate verdict line. The lines and bytes_of are checked against the reference on the corpus, not by proof

inventory.name: extraction/driver.ml
inventory.reason: DS-05: the hand-written command line (M-11): argument parsing, reading whole files, printing the returned strings; exit status 0 with a verdict, 1 for an unreadable input or one longer than a primitive string, 2 for bad usage, 3 when the computation fails (stack or memory exhausted)

inventory.name: OCaml 4.14.1 native compiler, runtime and standard library (TC-06, ocamlopt)
inventory.reason: DS-05 H-01: compiles the extracted code, Pstring, Uint63 and the driver to one x86-64 executable (assembled and linked by the host's gcc and binutils) with the OCaml runtime and standard library linked in; it loads only libc and libm

inventory.name: OCaml 4.14.1 bytecode compiler and standard library (TC-06, ocamlc)
inventory.reason: DS-05 H-02: compiles the same sources to one bytecode executable

inventory.name: OCaml 4.14.1 bytecode runtime for AArch64 (TC-10, ocamlrun)
inventory.reason: DS-05 H-02: interprets the checker's bytecode; its only file outside /usr at run time

inventory.name: qemu-user-static 8.2.2 (TC-08) with the AArch64 C library of TC-09
